description: Every image displayed in README.md or docs/, keyed by PNG basename under docs/images/. Producers are functions of scripts.docs_analytics modules; the Read the Docs build never runs them.

classes.paper_replication: A published figure regenerated offline by a registered producer that calls the paper module with the paper's parameters.
classes.paper_reproduction: A crop of a CC BY 4.0 figure of the IJTAF article whose inputs cannot be distributed; registered with the original producer and its data prerequisites.
classes.bundled_snapshot: Computed from an option chain bundled in the package, a dated historical quote set.
classes.synthetic: Drawn from the page's canonical script with fixed parameters and seed.

qvar_option_smiles.png.question: What skew do call options on quadratic variance have, and do the MMA and inverse valuations agree with simulation?

conventions.measure: MMA and inverse; Monte Carlo under MMA
conventions.data: Packaged QV chain get_qv_options_test_chain_data; forwards set to the expected QV and strikes to 75% to 150% of it, as plot_qvar_figure
conventions.reimplementation: article_figures.py imports qis, which is not a dependency; the producer computes the quantities of LogSVPricer.plot_comp_mma_inverse_options_with_mc and draws them with vol_slice_fit in two rows
conventions.simulation: 400,000 paths with 5,760 steps per year, seed 13 for the numba generator, through qv_option_mc_vols of the canonical script. The paper code uses 200,000 paths and seed 20 and passes no step count; with the current package the pricer then takes int(360 T) + 1 = 31 steps per year, and its Monte Carlo intervals (one week: 302% to 385%) match neither the transform values nor the published figure, whose intervals resemble the fine-step ones
conventions.error: Root-mean-square difference to the Monte Carlo implied volatility, labelled mse in the legend
conventions.existence: Theorem 4.3 guarantees the QV transform on Re(Psi) = -1/2 when kappa2 > vartheta; Eq. (6.4) has vartheta = 3.10 above kappa2 = 2.18
